question: Do observed anthropogenic resource expansion and, secondarily, host-contribution architecture depart from expectations generated by exact resolved host count and exact host-family composition alone?
eligible_species: Primary expansion null: all host-taxonomy-lower-bound adequate butterflies with sufficient within-family HOSTS-WCVP pools, including zero-expansion species. Secondary architecture diagnostics: observed-expanded species, with randomized architecture conditional on the randomized portfolio producing introduced-added units.

preserve_exactly: number of hosts in each WCVP host family
null.randomization: For each focal butterfly, sample without replacement the same number of alternative HOSTS-WCVP plant species from each of its observed host families, then reconstruct native and contemporary WGSRPD3 resource unions.
null.candidate_pool: All species-level HOSTS plant taxa resolved to WCVP in the same fixed reconstruction and having valid native and contemporary WCVP footprints.

primary_statistics: Across the full conservative panel: number of expanded species, mean and median log resource expansion, total introduced-added WGSRPD3 units, and Spearman(host-family breadth, log resource expansion)
Species-level observed log expansion and added units versus each species family-composition-matched null
Secondary only: effective contributor number and maximum single-host share among observed-expanded species
species_level_diagnostic: For every conservative-panel species, compare observed log expansion and absolute added units with its exact-family-composition matched null. Architecture comparisons are secondary and conditional on nonzero randomized expansion.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc robustness analysis motivated by manuscript review. It controls exact resolved host count and exact WCVP host-family composition but not evolutionary host accessibility, interaction-record completeness, geographic sampling bias or causal host choice. Architecture metrics remain structurally bounded by portfolio size and are secondary.
